\subsection{Class-AB Transimpedance Amplifier}\label{ss:tiaampab}

\texttt{anatop\_tia\_amp\_ab} is the amplifier of the transimpedance stage of
Section~\ref{ss:tiaamp}. The cell contains 34 devices and carries schematic, symbol,
layout and \texttt{av\_extracted} views; every figure and table in this section is
schematic-level, taken with no extracted parasitics.

The input stage is complementary and rail-to-rail: an NMOS and a PMOS differential
pair, both active at the \SI{1.25}{\volt} input common mode
(Figure~\ref{fig:tiaampab-topology}). Both pairs fold into cascode summing branches,
and the output stage is class~AB, with both output devices actively driven.
Compensation is of the cascode (Ahuja) form. The common-source node of the PMOS
cascodes, \texttt{C1}, and the common-source node of the NMOS cascodes, \texttt{C2},
are brought out as pins and the compensation capacitors sit outside the cell: one
from \texttt{C1} to \texttt{Out} and one from \texttt{C2} to \texttt{Out},
\SI{500}{\femto\farad} each in this characterisation. Compensation is therefore set
per application without editing the cell.

Bias is taken from the local bias generator of Section~\ref{ss:biasgen-local} over
the global rails \texttt{bn!}, \texttt{bnc!}, \texttt{bp!} and \texttt{bpc!}, at trim
code \texttt{BiasAdj}~=~37 for all data in this section.

Bench conditions are $R_f = \SI{560}{\kilo\ohm}$, $C_f = \SI{22}{\pico\farad}$, a
\SI{5}{\pico\farad} load, $v_{\mathrm{cm}} = \SI{1.25}{\volt}$ and a \SI{2.5}{\volt}
supply, with the working electrode loaded by the \texttt{randles\_cell} model of
Section~\ref{ss:analog-models} (Figure~\ref{fig:randles-cell}) at
$R_s = \SI{100}{\ohm}$, $R_{\mathrm{ct}} = \SI{1}{\mega\ohm}$,
$C_{\mathrm{dl}} = \SI{100}{\nano\farad}$. Only the \SI{560}{\kilo\ohm} tap of the
\SIrange{35}{560}{\kilo\ohm} programmable feedback string is characterised, and every
figure and table in this section is at that tap.

Coverage is five process points: the typical statistical section
\texttt{castalia\_pm\_25} at nominal, and ff, fs, sf and ss at \SI{25}{\celsius}.
Temperature is not uniform across benches. The closed-loop transimpedance bench runs
at \SI{37}{\celsius} at the typical point and in Monte Carlo, and at
\SI{25}{\celsius} at the four skew corners; the unity-gain, drive and power benches
run at \SI{25}{\celsius} throughout.
